memory_candidates.content: When a new reserved-sentinel admission dimension is added to a predicate whose comparison target already uses generic exact-match overlap detection (e.g. file_scope_collision's scopes_overlap_first), do not assume a 'new dimension evaluated LAST, only on an otherwise-admit candidate, no existing branch edited' design will actually be reachable -- two actors declaring the IDENTICAL sentinel literal already produce an ordinary exact match under the pre-existing predicate, so the existing branch intercepts the case first. The resolution that preserves non-regression is to RELABEL the existing branch's own already-selected match in place (inspect which value it matched on; branch the verdict SHAPE on that, not the selection logic) rather than bolt on a trailing, separately-evaluated stage. This generalizes to any future reserved-token admission dimension layered onto an overlap-style predicate.

When adding a new defer_reason/error-code/enum value to a producer whose documentation records that EVERY prior addition of the same kind required a matching case arm in a specific downstream consumer (a closed `case ... esac` with a loud default arm warning 'add a matching case arm here'), always grep that consumer for the enum's dispatch site BEFORE closing the implementation phase, even if the consumer script is outside the phase's own declared Files-to-modify list. The producer-side gate can work perfectly while the consumer silently mis-ledgers the new value into an 'unrecognized' bucket with a scary warning -- a correctness gap that is easy to miss because the gate's own tests never exercise the consumer at all.

In a shared concurrent working tree (multiple /orchestrate batch tasks dispatched at once), a generated-bookkeeping file regenerator (e.g. generate-context-line-counts.sh --write) that scans and corrects EVERY stale entry repo-wide will often also fix an unrelated entry caused by a concurrent sibling task's in-progress edit elsewhere. Before committing such a regenerator's output under your own task, diff the specific hunks and revert any that belong to a file your own task never touched -- otherwise you silently misattribute another task's fix to your own commit, and the sibling's own eventual regen run may reintroduce drift your revert should have left alone.
